moat_against: ROIC proxy collapsed: 12.0% (2022) → 6.7% (2023) → 0.1% (2024) → -0.7% (2025) — capital allocation is destroying the core's returns
Residential portal war: Homes.com fights Zillow's entrenched consumer network effect from behind; activists (Third Point, D.E. Shaw) called it a reckless drain before Third Point exited in Apr 2026
Acquisition spree at full prices — Matterport, Domain, Zonda (~$800M), OnTheMarket; goodwill jumped to 47% of assets in 2025
SBC more than doubled to $194M in 2025 (6.0% of revenue) and capex spiked on owned real estate (HQ tower, Richmond campus)
CRE transaction cyclicality (Ten-X volumes down) and founder-CEO concentration
moat_for: CoStar suite is the CRE industry data standard — 93% renewal rate, 327,000 subscribers +19% YoY (Q2 2026)
Proprietary property database accumulated over decades; workflow-embedded switching costs (89% overall renewal, 94% for customers of 5+ years)
Gross margin 79-82% sustained 2016-2025 — pricing power evidence
Network effects in LoopNet / Apartments.com marketplaces on the commercial and multifamily side
61 consecutive quarters of double-digit revenue growth (through Q2 2026)
moat_justification: Core CoStar suite is the commercial real estate data standard with 93% renewal (Q2 2026), 89% overall / 94% for 5yr+ customers, ~79-82% gross margins held for a decade, and a proprietary property database built over decades — but consolidated ROIC proxy fell from 9-12.5% (2019-2022) to 6.7% (2023), ~0% (2024) and -0.7% (2025) as capital poured into the Homes.com residential war against Zillow's entrenched network and into Matterport/Domain/Zonda acquisitions (goodwill 47% of assets in 2025). A 6 credits the durable core franchise without paying for returns the consolidated business is not currently earning.
name: CoStar Group, Inc.
one_liner: Dominant CRE data franchise, moat 6/10, but owner's earnings have been spent into the ground — TTM OE is $0.22/sh against a $32.31 price (weighted IRR 3.9%, weighted IV@15% $2.97); it does not clear 15% at any price above ~$3 on current OE, so the stock is a margin-recovery bet, not an OE compounder at this price.
